questions.topic: The standard error of a mean
questions.stem: For a integrated mathematics III homework set, explain standard error.

options.text: Standard error is sigma divided by square root of n.
Standard error is sigma times square root of n.
options.misconception: confuses "Standard error is sigma times square root of n" with the correct "Standard error is sigma divided by square root of n"

options.text: Standard error is sigma squared divided by n.
options.misconception: uses variance instead of standard deviation

options.text: Standard error is always zero for large n.
options.misconception: confuses "Standard error is always zero for large n" with the correct "Standard error is sigma divided by square root of n"

questions.explanation: The rule that settles this the standard error of a mean item is: Divide sigma by sqrt(n). That is why "Standard error is sigma divided by square root of n" is right. The option "Standard error is sigma times square root of n" (confuses "Standard error is sigma times square root of n" with the correct "Standard error is sigma divided by square root of n") does not satisfy the rule.
